h1: AI Model Photos and Videos for Fashion Brands, Without a Casting Day
lead: A flat garment photo can become a try-on, a fit check, or a short look. You skip the casting call and check the print before you post.
card: Try-ons, fit checks, lookbooks, and review-style clips from one garment photo.

faq.q: Can one garment photo make both a vertical clip and a listing image?
faq.a: Yes. Use 9:16 and 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds for a turn or a short walk, and the same photo for an on-model still. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120.

faq.q: Can a flat-lay photo become an on-model photo?
faq.a: Yes. Smooth the garment, shoot the whole piece in even light, and describe the person and the room. Check seams and hems before you list it.

faq.q: Will the print or the fabric change?
faq.a: The result follows your photo. Fine stripes, embroidery, and buttons stay closer when the upload is sharp. If a trim moves, make another version. A failed job returns its credits.

faq.q: Can I show a plus-size or petite model?
faq.a: Describe the person in plain words, including height, build, and age range. The model is generated. It is not a photo of a real customer.

faq.q: What photo works best for an on-model result?
faq.a: A flat lay or a hanger shot, whole garment visible, front side up, even light. Outline, color, print, and fastenings all need to be clear.

faq.q: How do I keep the fabric color accurate?
faq.a: Shoot in soft daylight, not under a warm lamp, and name the color in plain words. Compare the result with the garment before you publish.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid clothing ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid ads. Size and fabric claims have to match the real item.

faq.q: How is an on-model clip different from a creator?
faq.a: You pay the credits shown before the job, not a creator fee. The person is generated, so post it as an ad, not as a customer's review.
